title: publish-release.mjs reports the wrapper "published and verified" before a consumer can install it
description: Measured during the 0.7.1 publish, 2026-09-15. scripts/publish-release.mjs printed "@opum-ai/quest 0.7.1 published and verified (1 check)" and exited 0; at 16:03:02Z, seconds later, `npm install -g @opum-ai/quest@0.7.1` failed with notarget, a plain HTTPS read of registry.npmjs.org/@opum-ai/quest/0.7.1 returned "version not found: 0.7.1", the packument listed versions up to 0.7.0 with dist-tags latest 0.7.0, and the wrapper first resolved from a plain read at 16:04:06Z (packument time.modified 16:03:39Z). So the final verification passed inside a window in which a consumer install failed: the same class QCLI-299 closed for the platform packages (write success is not consumer visibility) is still open for the wrapper own post-publish verification, which apparently reads through a path that sees the write before the public read API does. Not urgent: the six platform packages were correctly gated, nothing was left uninstallable for more than about a minute, and the receipt:verify-published gate passed afterwards. It matters because the script output is what an operator stops on, and "verified" was said about a state a consumer could not yet see.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The wrapper post-publish verification reads the public registry over plain HTTPS with no credential and no npmrc, the same client the platform gate uses, and holds the same settle margin before declaring success

A test drives the failure on purpose: a wrapper whose write returned success but whose public packument does not yet list the version is reported as not-yet-visible, and the script does not print "published and verified" until a plain read resolves it
The runbook publish section states what "verified" means after this change and records the 0.7.1 measurement (about a minute between the script verification and the first public read)
